recipes.name: Risk It On Brisket
ingredients_raw: 1 (3 pound) beef brisket (first cut, or lean flat portion)

steps.text: Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).

Mix together the ketchup, ginger ale, dry onion soup mix, brown sugar, and red wine in a bowl, and stir until the brown sugar dissolves. Place the brisket into a disposable aluminum pan, and pour sauce over the brisket. Seal the pan with a cover of aluminum foil.
Bake in the preheated oven until the meat is very tender, about 4 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Risk It On Brisket
raw_recipe.description: A beef brisket is slathered with a sweet and tangy sauce, then baked slowly for tenderness and flavor. Use the flat, lean portion of a brisket (the first cut) for this recipe.

review.reviewBody: i love it all of my kids love it

Cooking method; temp and time? Spot on. Incredibly tender, nearly fall apart meat. The sauce…….was too sweet for my personal preference. I can’t tell if it was the ketchup, or the ketchup PLUS brown sugar and ginger ale or what. Did we like this? Yes. Made for New Years Day. Started at noon and done at 4pm. I think we just like a more smoky, savory style brisket. I do think others should try this!! I think it’s a good recipe; just not totally “right” for us. And very glad I tried. It was my first time making brisket in the oven, so I was pleasantly surprised at how good it turned out! Thanks JaJa0908!
Better than the restaurants! Made a day ahead and reheated when needed. Not even a scrap of leftovers.

It's got a good sauce, but this would do better in a slow cooker. The meat is a little dry, and does not fall apart very easily. Furthermore, they don't tell you that you should use a disposable pan because all the sugar is going to burn and will be a black mess as soon as you take the pan out of the oven.

I made a 3.5 lb cut over the fire while camping and people loved it. It got to 200 internal fairy quickly- an hour? Then I let it bake, keeping the pan bake temp under 215. I used two foil pans for extra durability. Let it go for 6 hours then broke it up with a spatula- it was so tender. Flipped once and at the end, the bottom was just starting to char. Served on Hawaiian rolls. Kids want me to make at home now.

I have never posted a review here, but this recipe deserves it! PHENOMENAL recipe! I have tried a few other brisket recipes that were just…ok. THIS one is delicious, easy, sooooo flavorful! I can’t wait to make it again for my son snd his girlfriend this weekend! After reading the other reviews, I decided to add minced garlic and liquid smoke. It turned out amazing!!!! Easy. Delicious. I highly, highly recommend!
This is a fabulous recipe. I had to alter the cooking time a bit at 5 1/2 hours for a nearly 6# Brisket.
Followed the recipe to a tee and it was excellent!

I wish I could have cut more of the fat off. I think that changed the flavor. The sauce was great with the brisket once I drained off the fat. I wish I cut the cooking time down so it would have been a little pink.

My family really liked this and gave it a 4.3 star!
My husband is gluten free, so I couldn't use the lipton onion soup mix, so I used a recipe to make my own. Used a 3+ Lb Brisket and cooked it for 4.5 hours. Their only complaint was it was missing a smokey flavor.
